title: Calculus III: Multivariable & Vector Calculus
description: Vector-valued geometry, partial derivatives, constrained optimization, multiple integrals, and vector calculus for fields, flux, and spatially distributed biological systems.

modifications: Linked the first four lesson objective pairs to course outcomes, corrected three item-to-objective associations, and added direct practice for vector components, stationary-point classification, and line-integral work.

outcomes.description: Represent vectors in frames, compute directional derivatives, and interpret gradients.
Optimize multivariable functions with and without constraints.
Set up multiple integrals in appropriate coordinates.
Relate line and surface integrals to vector-field theorems.
Verify branch, coordinate-coverage and integrability conditions before applying local derivatives, change of variables or integral theorems.

lesson_objectives.description: Represent vectors in coordinate frames.
Compute gradients and directional derivatives.
Classify stationary points using second derivatives.
Use Lagrange multipliers for a smooth geometric constraint.
Choose bounds for an area or volume integral.
Include the Jacobian in a coordinate change.
Interpret line integrals as work or circulation.
Choose Green's, Stokes', or divergence theorem from the geometry.
Compute partial derivatives and the gradient vector of a two-variable concentration field at a point.
Calculate a directional derivative, identify the direction of steepest ascent and interpret the gradient's magnitude.
Apply Fick's law J = −D∇C and estimate the fractional concentration difference across a cell to judge whether a gradient is detectable.
Find critical points of a two-variable function and classify them with the second-derivative (Hessian) test.
Solve a constrained optimization with a Lagrange multiplier and interpret the optimal design.
Set up and evaluate a double integral in polar coordinates, including the Jacobian factor r, for a radially symmetric quantity.
Compute vector lengths, projections and cross products in a stated frame.
Calculate speeds, unit tangents and traced curve lengths.
Interpret normal directions, distances and coordinate units.
Calculate partial and mixed derivatives with fixed-coordinate conditions.
Apply tangent planes and path chain rules.
Distinguish differentiability and bound a local linearization remainder.
Solve stationary equations and classify a Hessian.
Evaluate regular equality-constraint candidates and multiplier conventions.
Compare feasible stationary and boundary candidates.
Set up bounded multiple integrals from slice geometry.
Calculate transformed totals with absolute Jacobian factors.
Interpret measure, coordinate conventions and density averages.
Calculate scalar arc-length and oriented vector line integrals.
Use potential differences and test conservative-field conditions.
Relate planar circulation and curl under valid Green conditions.
Construct oriented surface area vectors and integrate flux.
Compare direct boundary and divergence-volume transfer.
Interpret flux signs, smoothness and closed-boundary conditions.
Use compatible boundary orientation in Stokes circulation.
Calculate source, sink and storage balances from signed transfer.
Select vector-field theorems with domain and model checks.
Summarize synthetic outward-normal densities and calculate area-weighted transfer.
Compare boundary and divergence balances under source and storage assumptions.
Interpret calibration effects, orientation and limits of sink identification.
Set up and solve the normal equations for a least-squares line and confirm the minimum with the second-derivative test.
Fit an exponential model by a log-linear least-squares line and explain how it differs from a direct fit.
Compute partial derivatives of constrained variables with the held variable stated, and check them with differentials or the triple-product rule.
Verify an implicit chart,its first derivatives and graph measure.
Recover second derivatives without freezing a varying denominator.
Combine graph derivatives with a constrained spatial path.
Distinguish local derivative,global branches and a regular curve with a failed graph coordinate.
Derive a nonlinear local measure factor and physical radius.
Distinguish covered area from distinct image area.
Track density composition,measure and multiplicity separately.
Choose global coordinate coverage rather than repairing an answer by an unexplained factor.
Compute iterated limits without assuming unproved order exchange.
Evaluate distinct simultaneous cutoff paths for a singular expression.
Prove failure of absolute integrability from a diverging lower-region integral.
Separate a chosen regularization from a valid ordinary order-independent integral.
Verify a distinct implicit derivative,finite change and linearization error.
Compare interior and boundary candidates for a global constrained result.
Derive transformed bounds,variable measure and density totals.
Verify a new global coverage count and target-region totals.
Close a complete curved-boundary flux and independent volume ledger.
Distinguish circulation,curl flux and scalar surface measure.
Separate order,cutoff convention and ordinary integrability.
Check signed loop multiplicities before invoking a surface theorem.

lessons.title: Vectors, partial derivatives, and gradients
lessons.worked_example: For the constructed dimensionless field f(x,y)=x²y+sin(y), the gradient at (1,0) is (0,2). Along the unit direction (3/5,4/5), the directional derivative is 1.6. A displacement (0.02,0.03) has first-order predicted change 0.06, close to the exact 0.06121 rather than equal to it. Under a 90-degree orthonormal rotation, gradient components (4,-3) and direction components (0.8,-0.6) retain the directional derivative 5.

lessons.title: Multivariable optimization and constraints
lessons.worked_example: For F(x,y)=4−(x−1)²−2(y+2)², the stationary point (1,−2) has Hessian diag(−2,−4) and is a strict global maximum of 4. For f=xy subject to x+y=10, the multiplier equations give (5,5), value 25; substitution gives f(x,10−x)=25−(x−5)², proving the global bound.

lessons.title: Multiple integrals and coordinate transforms
lessons.worked_example: For a radius-3 disk, polar integration with Jacobian r gives area 9π≈28.274, matching the Cartesian semicircle integral. A constructed density c(r)=2+r mg/cm² on a radius-2 disk integrates to 40π/3 mg; dividing by area 4π cm² gives mean density 10/3 mg/cm².

modules.title: Line integrals, flux, and integral theorems

lessons.title: Line integrals, flux, and integral theorems
lessons.worked_example: For F=(-y,x) on the counterclockwise unit circle, parameterization gives circulation 2π; Green's theorem independently gives the integral of curl 2 over disk area π. For F=(x,y,z), divergence 3 over the unit ball gives outward sphere flux 4π.

lessons.title: Gradients in a concentration field: partial derivatives, directional derivatives and what a cell can sense
lessons.worked_example: At (30, 40) μm the synthetic field is 60.65 μM with ∇C = (-0.7278, -0.9704) μM/μm and |∇C| = 1.213; the diagonal directional derivative is -1.2009; with D = 10 μm²/s the flux is 12.13, and a 10 μm cell sees a 20% difference.

lessons.title: Optimizing with and without constraints, and integrating over a disk in polar coordinates
lessons.worked_example: x² + xy + y² − 3x has a minimum -3 at (2, -1); a 100 cm³ closed cylinder of least area has r = 2.515 cm and h = 2r; the polar integral of the synthetic density over r ≤ 50 μm gives 618,060 molecules, 39.3% of the total.

lessons.title: Vectors, planes and spatial curves
lessons.worked_example: For the helix, differentiate all three coordinates rather than treating z as constant. The horizontal contribution to squared speed is 9(sin²t+cos²t)=9, and the vertical contribution is 16. Thus speed is constantly 5 and length over [0,2] is 10. Divide the derivative by 5 to obtain the unit tangent, with vertical component 0.8. For a plane calculation, use the independent normal (2,−1,2), divide its residual by length 3, and obtain an origin-to-plane distance of 2. The same normalization principle supports both calculations, but tangent and plane normal are different geometric objects.

lessons.title: Partial derivatives and total change
lessons.worked_example: For f=x²y+sin y, compute coordinate derivatives before evaluating them. At (2,0), f_x=0, f_y=5 and f_xy=4. The displacement (0.1,0.02) gives a tangent prediction of 0.1. Along the different path x=1+t,y=t² at t=1, evaluate the partials at (2,1) and include both path velocities, giving 13.080605. These values differ because the derivative questions differ. One concerns a local plane near (2,0), and the other concerns a moving point at (2,1).

lessons.title: Hessians, constraints and boundary optima
lessons.worked_example: First solve the unconstrained quadratic equations to get (1,1), classify it using D=8 and record value −6. Then impose the rectangle. Discard the infeasible stationary point, solve all four edge problems, and compare −35/6, −16/3, −1.75 and −4. The smallest is −35/6 at (0.5,7/6). The constrained minimum is higher than the unconstrained one, as expected when a feasible set is made smaller. This scale check catches an alleged constrained value below −6 for this particular objective.

lessons.title: Multiple integrals and Jacobian measures
lessons.worked_example: For the elliptical region, substitute x=2u,y=3v, find determinant 6 and transform the boundary into u²+v²≤1. Integrate 6 over the unit disk to obtain 6π. For the ball, integrate the spherical angular factor sinφ from zero to π, giving 2, and azimuth over a full turn, giving 2π. The remaining radial integrals are ∫₀²ρ²dρ for volume and ∫₀²ρ⁴dρ for the density total. The common angular factor is 4π, while the different radial powers answer different questions.

modules.title: Line integrals, potentials and Green's theorem

lessons.title: Line integrals, potentials and Green's theorem
lessons.worked_example: Compare the gradient field (2xy,x²) and rotation field (−y,x). For the first, identify φ=x²y and use endpoint differences, obtaining 4 for (0,0) to (2,1). For the second, a counterclockwise unit circle has curl integral 2 times disk area, or 2π, and a direct parameter calculation agrees. Now change to the vortex field: the circle integral still equals 2π, although local curl is zero away from the origin. The missing origin prevents using the disk as a smooth theorem region. Formula, orientation and domain all contribute to the answer.

modules.title: Surface flux and the divergence theorem

lessons.title: Surface flux and the divergence theorem
lessons.worked_example: For the sloped patch z=x+y, compute the cross product of (1,0,1) and (0,1,1) to get (−1,−1,1). Its magnitude is √3, establishing area √3 over a unit parameter square. Dot the vertical field (0,0,z) into that area vector to obtain integrand x+y and total 1. For the diffusion sphere, use the outward normal r/2, so J·n=−2. Integrate over area 16π to obtain −32π and compare with the divergence-volume result. The first surface is open and oriented upward; the second is closed and oriented outward.

lessons.title: Stokes' theorem and spatial balances
lessons.worked_example: For J=(−2x,−3y,−4z), the three positive-coordinate faces of the box contribute −4, −6 and −8; the zero-coordinate faces contribute zero. Their sum is −18, matching divergence −9 times volume 2. Insert this signed result into storage balance. A uniform sink 9 gives steady storage, while sink 12 gives storage loss 6. For the tilted triangle and the separate circulation field F, use its oriented area vector rather than unsigned area to obtain 1/2. Transfer and circulation use related geometric machinery but represent different integrals.

modules.title: Least-squares fitting and partial derivatives with non-independent variables

lessons.title: Least-squares fitting and partial derivatives with non-independent variables
lessons.worked_example: For synthetic points (0, 1), (1, 3), (2, 4) and (3, 6), the normal equations 14a + 6b = 29 and 6a + 4b = 14 give a = 1.6 and b = 1.1; the Hessian determinant 80 confirms the minimum, the residuals sum to zero and the minimum squared error is 0.20. For w = xyz with z = x + y at (1, 2, 3), differentials give (∂w/∂x)_y = 8 and (∂w/∂x)_z = 3.

modules.title: Virtual lab 1: oriented boundary flux and a steady volume balance

lessons.title: Virtual lab 1: oriented boundary flux and a steady volume balance
lessons.worked_example: The six-face synthetic boundary has corrected outward transfer −18 amount units per second, matching divergence −9 times volume 2. A known density offset contributes 10 separately. Interpreting the inward supply as a uniform sink of 9 additionally requires steady storage and no source; the field alone establishes no real tissue consumption.

lessons.title: Field project guide: amount and outward transfer in a bounded concentration field (optional, ungraded)
lessons.worked_example: For c(x, y) = 5 − (x² + y²) on the unit disk with D = 1 m²/s, the maximum is 5 at the center and the boundary value 4; the polar total is 4.5π ≈ 14.14 amount, and J = (2x, 2y) gives the same outward transfer, 4π ≈ 12.57 amount/s, from the boundary integral and from the divergence integral.

modules.title: Implicit branches and local surface charts

lessons.title: Implicit branches and local surface charts
lessons.worked_example: Since Fz=two z is nonzero, the upper local graph has gx=minus x/z=minus one half and gy=minus y/z=minus one. The scalar graph factor is sqrt(one+one/four+one)=three/two. A chart factor converts projected area to surface area; it is not another flat coordinate determinant.

lessons.title: Nonlinear Jacobians and global coverage
lessons.worked_example: The derivative determinant is four(u²+v²), so its point value is eight. The image is(zero, two), with radius two. Local positive orientation and a valid determinant do not yet establish how often the full input domain covers the target.

modules.title: Singular integrals, order and cutoff evidence

lessons.title: Singular integrals, order and cutoff evidence
lessons.worked_example: For fixed positive x, the y antiderivative y/(x²+y²)gives inner value one/(one+x²), then pi/four. For fixed positive y, the x antiderivative minus x/(x²+y²)gives the negative result. The disagreement signals a missing hypothesis rather than a contradiction of an applicable theorem.

modules.title: Assignment 1: implicit change and constrained extrema

lessons.title: Assignment 1: implicit change and constrained extrema
lessons.worked_example: The partials are minus one/(two sqrt2)and minus one/sqrt2. Their linear contributions cancel, so the tangent value remains sqrt2. The true value is sqrt2.005, and error is the unrounded difference, also 0.005/[sqrt2.005+sqrt2]. Display rounding is separate from this mathematical error.

modules.title: Assignment 2: nonlinear transform and coverage evidence

lessons.title: Assignment 2: nonlinear transform and coverage evidence
lessons.worked_example: The inverse is v=y, u=x/y and physical bounds one<=y<=three, y<=x<=two y. Determinant v varies across the domain. Area is four, total six and average1.5; the point determinant is two. Replacing the full factor by one point value would change the integral.

modules.title: Assignment 3: curved boundary and field evidence

lessons.title: Assignment 3: curved boundary and field evidence
lessons.worked_example: The upper graph area vector is(two x, two y, one)dA and F dot it is four−r^four, integrating to eleven pi/three. The bottom contributes minus pi, giving eight pi/three. Volume is pi/two; independent integration of divergence four z gives the same complete flux.

lessons.title: Assignment 4: domain and limit dossier
lessons.worked_example: The iterated values are plus/minus pi/four. The ratio-three rectangle tends to atan3−pi/four=atan(one half), which is different from both and from the balanced cutoff zero. Each finite rectangle is regular; the excluded-corner limit needs its own convention because absolute integrability fails.

grading_policy.attempt_policy: Unlimited formative retries; no summative grade is awarded.
grading_policy.solution_release: Public practice solutions may be shown after an attempt. They are not production exam keys.
grading_policy.late_policy: No deadlines or late penalties exist in this partial package.

known_issues: Unicode equations require structured mathematical alternatives and assistive-technology review.

history.summary: Preserved original compact prototype content in separate manifests and readings; labeled partial without semester or credit equivalency.

Added an original lesson on gradients in a concentration field (partial and directional derivatives, steepest ascent, Fick's law and gradient detectability across a cell) with synthetic data, formative items with computed keys and retrieval cards. The package remains partial and unreviewed.

Added an original lesson on unconstrained and Lagrange-multiplier optimization and polar double integrals with synthetic data, formative items with computed keys and retrieval cards. The package remains partial and unreviewed.

Assessments with items now also list the course outcomes those items assess, derived from each item's lesson objective and that objective's outcome links. The rubric-only case lists none, and neither do the 4 prototype-unit assessments, whose objectives are not yet linked to an outcome. No readings, items or keys changed. The syllabus was regenerated from the manifest: it states the current version, lists every lesson with its item and card counts, and describes the current practice and limitations (it still described only the four original units). The course limitations shown to learners were also updated: they still described one formative check per lesson and the original numerical rules. The package remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Added seven original lessons on vector geometry, total multivariable change, Hessians and constrained boundaries, Jacobian measures, line integrals and Green, surface flux and divergence, and Stokes with spatial balances; one synthetic flux-balance lab and a proposed 14-week schedule. Developed with Codex assistance using existing scope references only. Still partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Expanded the vectors and gradients reading with a first-order local model, unit-direction derivatives, level-curve geometry and a worked finite-change comparison. Existing public questions, keys and objectives are unchanged. Three compact prototype readings remain; the package stays partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Expanded the week-5 optimization reading with second-derivative classification, a negative-definite Hessian example, Lagrange multipliers and a direct global-bound check along the feasible set. Existing questions, keys and objectives are unchanged. Two compact prototype readings remain; the package stays partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Expanded the week-8 multiple-integral reading with change-of-variables Jacobians, polar area and a spatially varying density example with units. Existing questions, keys and objectives are unchanged. One compact prototype reading remains; the package stays partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Expanded the week-10 reading with parameterized line integrals, Green circulation and flux forms, and distinctions among Green, Stokes and divergence theorems. Existing questions, keys and objectives are unchanged. All scheduled lessons now have expanded or original instructional text; the package remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Linked the first four lesson objective pairs to outcomes 1–4, clarified outcome 1 to include vector-frame representation, corrected three item associations, and added direct formative checks for vector components, stationary-point classification, and line-integral work. Existing numeric prompts and keys are unchanged. The course remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Expanded the vector-and-gradient lesson with a worked orthonormal-frame rotation showing that a directional derivative is unchanged when the gradient and direction are represented consistently. Existing question prompts, answer keys, objectives and cards are unchanged. The package remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Added an inactive, ungraded integrative vector-field project draft with a circular concentration model, constrained extrema, polar area integration, oriented boundary flux, an independent divergence check and an unweighted human rubric. The project is not part of the scheduled assessment list. The course remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Integrated a multistep region, orientation and theorem-selection sequence into the existing week-13 Stokes lesson: planar circulation, a closed cylindrical flux with direct face checks, and an open-cap boundary. Added six formative items and three cards, and linked the recommended Linear Algebra frame/coordinate refresher. The course remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Grouped an original least-squares and held-variable reading with the week-6 Hessian lesson: normal equations and their second-derivative check, log-linear exponential fits compared with a direct fit, and partial derivatives of constrained variables by differentials and the triple-product rule. Added three objectives, eleven formative items and four cards, with no week added. The course remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Made the planned concentration-and-flux field project usable by learners as ungraded practice. Week 13 gains an optional project guide with the project's field, region, diffusivity and five tasks, a worked example on a separate field, the draft's published construction checks, a rehearsal field and four open rehearsal practice items; five project milestones are Case studio self-checks with a week-14 project record. The boundary-flux lab's dataset link now points to the package-pinned CSV instead of a mutable repository URL, and the week-13 reading's link to a Linear Algebra lesson now opens that lesson in the application. The inactive project draft is unchanged; the course remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Added three original implicit-chart/fold,nonlinear-Jacobian/coverage and singular-order/cutoff foundations with four connected reports and twenty checkpoints/cards. Developed curved complete-boundary flux/Stokes/area evidence and local-versus-global hypotheses,with one explicit outcome. Corrected the categorical no-compact-primer claim;all examples remain original synthetic mathematics and package partial,unreviewed and formative-only.

limitations: All scheduled lessons have expanded or original instructional text, alongside one synthetic flux-balance lab; this package is not equivalent to a full university semester.

The proposed 14-week schedule is unmeasured and unreviewed. Graded homework, exams, a laboratory sequence and a cumulative graded project remain absent. An optional concentration-and-flux field project guide with rehearsal practice and Case studio milestone self-checks (weeks 13–14) is ungraded practice; the separate project draft stays inactive.
Formative items and provisional objective associations do not establish comprehensive coverage or mastery.
All numerical fields, observations and balance rates are synthetic. They establish no tissue oxygen demand, device specification, unique biological mechanism or experimental protocol.

New numeric prompts state their scales and request a bare number. Existing unit-entry requirements are preserved; only the 7 numeric fields in the project rehearsal check significant figures, and dimensions are not automatically assessed.
CSV summaries and structured choices check selected calculations and interpretations, not written proofs or causal model identification.
Theorems and error bounds require their stated domains, smoothness, orientations, coordinate conventions and regularity conditions.
Qualified mathematical review, accessibility review and total/weekly workload measurement remain outstanding.
The new theorem-selection sequence uses exact synthetic fields and canonical regions; its checks reinforce calculation and hypotheses but do not replace proofs or broad theorem applications.

The concentration-and-flux field project is optional and ungraded. Its five milestones are Case studio self-checks whose private drafts are never submitted or scored; the rehearsal practice uses a separate field, and no software check evaluates a learner's derivation, figure or written interpretation. Milestone weeks are planning suggestions, not measured workload or deadlines.

Three foundations and four open reports develop local implicit charts/folds, nonlinear Jacobian coverage, signed singular-order/cutoff conditions, global constrained comparisons and curved-boundary flux/curl/area. These selected polynomial/singular counterexamples clarify calculus hypotheses rather than delivering general manifold, complex-analysis, topology or measure-theory courses. Broader coursework, workload and qualified review remain open.

Every function, density, map, region and path is a synthetic mathematical construction. Local nonvanishing conditions do not imply global uniqueness or once-only coverage; balanced singular cutoffs need not define an ordinary integral. Checkpoints assess selected values and interpretations, not proofs, code, plots, full reports or physical flux/source laws.

Of the 131 numerical answers, 3 require units, 55 check significant figures and 0 check dimensions. New continuous fields request three significant figures in named normalized units; exact branch, coverage and maximizing-point counts have no significant-figure requirement. Keep full intermediate precision when calculating a small approximation error.
intentionally_omitted: Graded assessments, a full laboratory sequence, a cumulative graded project, measured workload and qualified human review remain outstanding.
